<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518913852_theRebbe_463" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518913852_theRebbe_463__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Human service can elevate even the past, and Adam's service on Rosh Hashanah perfected all of creation retroactively.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And the explanation of the matter</t>
    <t s="2">(that Rosh Hashanah,</t>
    <t s="3">the day when the first man was created,</t>
    <t s="4">is the beginning of Your works)</t>
    <t s="5">in a deeper sense,</t>
    <t s="6">it is known that the service of man has the power to change even the past.</t>
    <t s="7">And from this it is understood</t>
    <t s="8">(all the more so)</t>
    <t s="9">regarding the service of the first man, who was the handiwork of the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="10">that the elevation he effected in all created beings through his proclamation, "Come, let us bow down... before Hashem our Maker," also applies to their existence prior to his service.</t>
    <t s="11">For since</t>
    <t s="12">the original intent of creation was that man, through his service, should draw down a revelation of G-dliness into the world,</t>
    <t s="13">therefore,</t>
    <t s="14">after a revelation of G-dliness is drawn into the world, an elevation is thereby effected also in the existence of the world that preceded it,</t>
    <t s="15">and especially since its purpose is the preparation for the revelation that is drawn down through the service of man.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The day of Rosh Hashanah is the beginning of all works, including the first five days of creation, because Adam's service elevated and renewed them.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this is what [is meant by] the day of Rosh Hashanah,</t>
    <t s="1">the day when the first man was created,</t>
    <t s="2">is the beginning of Your works,</t>
    <t s="3">for the simple explanation</t>
    <t s="4">(and a matter does not depart from its simple meaning)</t>
    <t s="5">[is that] "the beginning of Your works" is the beginning of all the works,</t>
    <t s="6">even the works that were in the first five days of creation</t>
    <t s="7">(including also the time of those days),</t>
    <t s="8">for through the service of the first man, an elevation and renewal was effected also in the existence of the world that preceded this,</t>
    <t s="9">and therefore this day is the beginning of Your works,</t>
    <t s="10">the beginning of all of creation.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Just as on the first Rosh Hashanah Adam's service perfected creation anew, so too each year Israel's coronation of Hashem perfects and renews all of creation, even above.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And just as on the first Rosh Hashanah,</t>
    <t s="1">on the day when the first man was created,</t>
    <t s="2">the perfection of creation was effected</t>
    <t s="3">(Your works),</t>
    <t s="4">and in a manner of renewal</t>
    <t s="5">(the beginning of Your works),</t>
    <t s="6">so too is it on Rosh Hashanah of every single year,</t>
    <t s="7">for through Israel crowning the Holy One, blessed be He, that He be King over them and over the entire world,</t>
    <t s="8">perfection and renewal are effected in all of creation,</t>
    <t s="9">and even to the extent that through this, perfection and renewal are effected also above,</t>
    <t s="10">according to the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov</t>
    <t s="11">and the Alter Rebbe</t>
    <t s="12">on the statement of the Mishnah,</t>
    <t s="13">"Know what is above from you,"</t>
    <t s="14">[meaning] that all the matters that are above are from you.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
